transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE); Samira Patel (Redwood SE); Aisha Khan (MediWave CTO); Ben Ortiz (MediWave ML Eng); Dana Li (MediWave DevOps)

Summary: Quick review of this week's benchmark run comparing Redwood POC cluster against the baseline provider that MediWave is using. Covered p50/p95 latency, throughput in tokens/sec, and tuning options including batching, KV cache, and int8 quantization. Some network noise noted on the baseline that affected p99. Ended with concrete next steps to run a private VPC soak and an ask for more sample payloads.

[00:00] Jordan: All right, thanks everyone for joining. can you hear me okay?
[00:03] Aisha: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks Jordan.
[00:05] Jordan: Great. Quick agenda: i want to run through the benchmark sheet we shared, call out differences vs your baseline provider, talk about tuning we did this week, and agree next steps. Samira is going to walk the numbers.
[00:15] Samira: Cool. So the key run was on the redwood-poc-cluster with our default batching and KV cache enabled. Model used was a 7B open model (note: misc transcribed as seven bee), sequence length avg ~256 tokens, peak window we tried to match your traffic pattern around 9am.
[00:30] Samira: p50 latency for token generation was ~120ms on our cluster, p95 was ~360ms. Throughput measured ~1,150 tokens/sec sustained on a 4-GPU pod. BaselineCloud in your sheet shows p50 ~180ms, p95 ~640ms and throughput ~780 tokens/sec under the same synthetic workload.
[01:00] Ben: those numbers look promising. curious what the batch sizes were and if you were using accumulation?
[01:10] Samira: We used adaptive batching with target batch size 32 for that run, intermittent accumulation for short sequences. Enabled KV cache prefix caching which cut off about ~18% of repeated token compute. We also tested int8 quantized run - the int8 run showed a further 25-30% throughput improvement but added a small quality delta we flagged in the notes.
[01:35] Aisha: small quality delta how small? do you have examples?
[01:40] Samira: We included a short eval set - hallucination and instruction-following were within expected variance; a couple of prompts produced slightly shorter completions, might be prompt-tuning fixable. I can share the eval rows.
[01:55] Jordan: also worth calling out noise in the baseline runs - we saw network jitter during their run window which may have bumped their p95. Ben, do you remember if those baseline runs were in the same region?
[02:08] Ben: yeah baseline was us-west2 but they were on a shared noisy host for part of the run, so that may explain some p99 delta. we noted that in the sheet.
[02:18] Dana: also for production we care about tail latencies more than average. what's your p99 look like on redwood in these runs?
[02:25] Samira: p99 was ~720ms on the standard run, on the int8 run p99 increased to ~850ms because quantization made some kernel paths slower for long contexts. But with tuned batching policy for tails we can get p99 down to ~600ms. that's with aggressive pre-warming and smaller max batch sizes for short-latency routes.
[02:50] Aisha: are those pre-warms compatible with dedicated/reserved capacity? our goal is predictable latency in peak windows.
[02:58] Samira: yes, on Redwood Dedicated you can pin a pool and use warmers; we also support conservative burst policies so you have steady baseline and short bursts. For private deployment the same runtime semantics apply - the control plane just instructs the nodes.
[03:15] Jordan: i want to call out a real-world spike test we ran - a 2-minute ramp to 3x baseline traffic. Redwood sustained throughput with p95 under 500ms; baseline provider had p95 blow out to 1.2s and dropped requests. That was one of the key differentiators in the sheet.
[03:35] Ben: interesting - what were the memory/kv cache hit rates in that spike?
[03:40] Samira: kv cache hit rate jumped to ~40% for repeated prefixes in that workload which helped reduce recompute. Memory utilization was stable; we tuned the eviction to favor recent sessions.
[03:50] Aisha: what's the impact on cost - doing all that caching and smaller batches sounds like it might raise unit cost.
[03:57] Jordan: good question. our Optimize toolkit predicted net cost savings by ~12% because KV cache reduces token compute and better batching increases GPU utilization. We put the cost model in the spreadsheet. also quantization can reduce GPU cost further but there is the small quality tradeoff Samira mentioned.
[04:20] Dana: on the topic of private deployment: network egress and VPC peering - will you need us to open any specific ports or setup special routing?
[04:28] Samira: For a VPC private pilot we'll need a couple of routes and an SSH bastion for initial setup; we provided a checklist in the security doc. No heavy egress requirements beyond typical gRPC endpoints. We'll send the exact terraform snippets.
[04:40] Jordan: we've already uploaded SOC2 and ISO artifacts to the shared drive but we'll also give you the redwood-private compliance pack and an HSM/KMS integration note if you want customer-managed keys.
[04:50] Aisha: great, security is one of the blockers. also need to check audit log retention and SSO.
[04:55] Samira: audit logs supported to customer retention limits; we can push longer retention for Dedicated or Private with enterprise package. SSO SAML works with SCIM provisioning. we'll include that in the package.
[05:08] Ben: one thing i noticed in the sheet - the baseline provider uses a different tokenizer which changes token counts for some prompts. were your tokenization settings aligned?
[05:18] Samira: yes we used the same tokenizer model and verified token counts on the eval set. there is still small variance for some multi-byte characters but we accounted for that in the cost calc.
[05:28] Aisha: curious about model fallbacks - if a pinned model gets overloaded, will Redwood automatically route to a compatible variant?
[05:34] Samira: yes that's part of smart routing: we can route by latency or cost policy and do automatic fallback to a compatible model variant. for POCs we usually keep routing conservative.
[05:45] Jordan: ok let's talk timeline for the private VPC soak. proposed: mediwave provisions VPC sandbox by 7/21, we run a 2-hour soak the week of 7/27, and then we reconvene for a demo and results review. does that sound reasonable?
[06:00] Dana: that works for ops. i'll schedule provisioning this week.
[06:05] Ben: can you include a test plan template? we'll map our SRE test cases.
[06:09] Samira: yes i'll attach a template; it includes traffic patterns, perturbation scripts, and the eval harness.
[06:15] Aisha: pricing - can you reiterate pilot pricing and estimated monthly spend for the Dedicated commit sizing?
[06:22] Jordan: sure. for the pilot we recommended a small commit (2-GPU equivalent) and hourly pilot pricing in the sheet. estimated monthly cost for production-sized committed capacity at your peak is in the range we emailed; i'll re-send a line-item with delta vs baseline provider.
[06:40] Aisha: last question on logs and data retention - do you store any customer payloads in the hosted mode? we need to ensure PHI is not persisted.
[06:48] Samira: hosted API by default has usage logs but can be configured for no retention; Private keeps logs in your control. for PHI we're recommending Private deployment or encrypted bring-your-own-key configs.
[06:58] Jordan: great. quick recap of next steps: I will send the updated benchmark sheet and pricing by Friday, Samira will share quantization test plan and test harness, MediWave will provision VPC sandbox and share payloads. We'll schedule the soak for week of 7/27 and run the int8 test on the pilot environment.
[07:18] Aisha: thanks everyone.
[07:20] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up in email.

End of meeting.
